result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with a large brick apartment building and standard pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks and signals. While sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the environment is complicated by embedded trolley tracks and parked cars that may obstruct sightlines at the crossing.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks embedded in the roadway can be slippery when wet and pose a tripping hazard for pedestrians or a crash risk for cyclists.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk limit the visibility between pedestrians entering the roadway and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the curb line

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they step into the travel lane.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for both drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and curb ramps with tactile paving, set within a residential neighborhood. However, the lack of dedicated pedestrian signals at a signalized intersection and visual obstructions from parked cars near the crossing reduce overall safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb near the crosswalk block sightlines between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the curb line leading to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection is controlled by a traffic light for vehicles but lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads, creating uncertainty for crossing pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection on the signal pole

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install countdown pedestrian signals to provide clear right-of-way information for people crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with a corner commercial property and residential buildings. While sidewalks and a marked crosswalk are present, the environment lacks traffic control signals and suffers from visual obstructions due to parked vehicles near the crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Cars parked close to the intersection corner block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line leading up to the crosswalk on the right side of the image.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No visible stop signs or signals at the intersection to regulate vehicle flow and provide dedicated crossing time for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and physically prevent illegal parking near the corner.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing crosswalk to a high-visibility 'continental' pattern to increase driver awareness.
